# Security & Auth Correctness Checklist: User Login

**Purpose**: Validate that the Login feature's requirements (spec.md, plan.md, contracts/auth-api.md)
are complete, unambiguous, and internally consistent on enumeration resistance, brute-force
lockout, token/session handling, password/transport security, and auditability — before
implementation begins.
**Created**: 2026-08-26
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [contracts/auth-api.md](../contracts/auth-api.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Enumeration Resistance

- [ ] CHK001 Are all three rejection cases (unregistered email, wrong password, deactivated account) explicitly required to produce an identical response, rather than merely "similar" or "generic"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the response required to be identical at the transport level (status code + body), not just the visible UI message — e.g., is a differing HTTP status code (404 vs 401) between "email not found" and "wrong password" explicitly ruled out? [Gap, Spec §FR-004, Contract §POST /auth/login]
- [ ] CHK003 Is response-timing consistency (avoiding a timing side-channel that reveals whether the email lookup vs. password comparison was the failing step) addressed, or explicitly noted as out of scope? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the requirement set specify whether the lockout response (423) is itself distinguishable from the generic 401 in a way that reintroduces enumeration (i.e., does reaching the "distinct lockout message" state leak that the email exists, and is that tradeoff explicitly acknowledged)? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications, Contract §423 Locked]

## Brute-Force Lockout

- [ ] CHK005 Is "consecutive" failed attempts precisely defined (e.g., does any successful login anywhere reset the counter, or only a login for that specific account)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the lockout window's start/end boundary condition specified (e.g., is a login attempt made at the exact millisecond of expiry treated as locked or unlocked)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the spec define what happens to the failure counter for attempts made *while already locked* — do they further extend the lock, get ignored, or still increment the counter invisibly? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, Data Model §Login Attempt Record]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the per-IP rate-limiting threshold/window left fully unspecified by design (deferred to planning), and is that deferral explicit rather than silently assumed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements defined for what a legitimate user sees/can do if they are locked out but need urgent access (e.g., is there any stated escalation path), or is "wait 15 minutes" the complete and only specified remedy? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK010 Is it specified whether lockout state is visible/queryable by an admin (e.g., for support purposes) or entirely opaque outside the locked user's own login attempts? [Gap]

## Token & Session Handling

- [ ] CHK011 Is the access token's storage location (in-memory only, never persisted) stated as a hard requirement rather than an implementation preference, and is the security rationale (XSS exposure) documented? [Clarity, Plan §Constitution Check, Research §2]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the refresh-token cookie attributes (`Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`) each individually required, rather than bundled into a vague "secure cookie" phrase that could be satisfied while omitting one attribute? [Clarity, Contract §POST /auth/login, PRD NFR]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the exact "Remember Me" duration (30 days) and the exact default (non-Remember-Me) session duration both specified with equal precision, or does one remain vague relative to the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK014 Are requirements defined for what happens to an *already-issued* refresh token when "Remember Me" was NOT checked but the browser is never closed (i.e., is there any absolute cap, or does the session persist indefinitely as long as the tab stays open)? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK015 Is token revocation scope precisely defined for every triggering event (logout = one session; deactivation = all sessions; role/status change = ?) so there's no ambiguity about how many sessions each event revokes? [Clarity/Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-011, Data Model §Session]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the spec/contract define the client's required behavior when a refresh attempt fails (401) — is "redirect to /login" the complete requirement, or are there unspecified intermediate states (e.g., retry, silent failure) left to interpretation? [Completeness, Spec Edge Cases, Contract §POST /auth/refresh-token]
- [ ] CHK017 Is "re-validated against the user's current role and status on every request" quantified enough to be verifiable (e.g., does it mean a live check on every single API call with no caching window, or is a bounded staleness window permitted)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-010]

## Password & Transport Security

- [ ] CHK018 Are password-hashing requirements (algorithm class, salting) referenced from this feature's requirements at all, or entirely deferred to the Account Creation/Password Change features with no cross-reference here? [Gap/Traceability]
- [ ] CHK019 Is "never logged in plaintext" (or transmitted outside the login request) stated as a requirement of THIS feature's logging/activity-log behavior specifically, not just inherited implicitly from the broader PRD? [Traceability, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK020 Is TLS-only transport stated as a requirement this feature's own contract must satisfy (e.g., cookie `Secure` flag, redirect-off-HTTP), or only as a general deployment assumption with no concrete, checkable requirement in this feature's scope? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK021 Does the spec/contract address what should happen if a login request somehow arrives over plain HTTP (reject vs. silently upgrade), or is this left undefined? [Gap]

## Auditability

- [ ] CHK022 Is the full set of loggable event types closed and unambiguous (login success, login failure, lockout, logout) with no undefined "etc.", so an implementer can't reasonably omit one? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK023 For a login failure against an unregistered email, is it specified what identifies the log entry in place of an account ID (e.g., the submitted email, hashed or raw) — or is this left ambiguous in a way that could itself leak/store sensitive data? [Gap/Ambiguity, Data Model §Activity Log Entry]
- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements explicit that the Activity Log must NEVER contain the attempted/actual password in any form (not just "not logged in logs" generically, but specifically ruling out the Activity Log record itself)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK025 Is retention/access-control for the Activity Log (who can view login/lockout audit entries) addressed by this feature's requirements, or explicitly noted as owned by a separate feature? [Gap/Traceability]

## Requirement Consistency & Dependencies

- [ ] CHK026 Do the spec (product-level) and the contract (contracts/auth-api.md, plan-level) agree on every status code / message pairing (401 generic, 423 locked), with no contradictory wording between the two documents? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the dependency on `buildcore-api` changes (currently a bare starter lacking these security behaviors, per research.md §1) explicitly flagged as a blocking prerequisite for this feature's acceptance scenarios, rather than assumed already satisfied? [Dependency, Research §1]
